t: You're at the north entrance to the North Wing of St Thomas' Hospital, on Lambeth Palace Road, looking at a statue of Edward VI. It's one of two statues of the king here, both marking his re-founding of the hospital in 1551. It was carved by the stonemason Thomas Cartwright in 1682, to a design by Nathaniel Hanwell. It once stood at the centre of a group of figures above the gateway on Borough High Street, and was moved here in the twentieth century. It is Grade Two star listed.
